statement: Vaccines (including MMR, thimerosal-containing, and cumulative antigen exposure) are not associated with autism spectrum disorder.
effect_size: No association across >1.2 million children pooled; nationwide cohorts of 537k (Madsen 2002) and 657k (Hviid 2019) both null, including in higher-risk subgroups
population: Meta-analysis of case-control and cohort studies, >1.2M children; multiple nationwide registries

provenance.primary: Taylor LE et al., 'Vaccines are not associated with autism: an evidence-based meta-analysis', Vaccine 2014; corroborated by Madsen NEJM 2002, Hviid Ann Intern Med 2019, Jain JAMA 2015, DeStefano J Pediatr 2013, Madsen Pediatrics 2003 (thimerosal)

confidence_notes: Decisively refuted at the highest tier. The origin (Wakefield Lancet 1998, n=12) was retracted for fraud (Lancet 2010, PMID 20137807) and the author struck off. This is a CLOSED question, not a 'both sides' debate. Cross-ref Section 26.

statement: The 1998 Wakefield Lancet paper claiming an MMR-autism link was based on 12 children, involved undisclosed financial conflicts and data manipulation, and was fully retracted; it provides no valid evidence of any vaccine-autism link.
effect_size: Origin study retracted; author erased from UK medical register for dishonesty

provenance.primary: Editors of The Lancet, 'Retraction--Ileal-lymphoid-nodular hyperplasia, non-specific colitis, and pervasive developmental disorder in children', Lancet 2010

confidence_notes: The foundational 'evidence' for the vaccine-autism myth never existed. Classic Rule-2 case: a fraudulent mechanism story became a dangerous public-health movement.

statement: Chelation therapy for autism has no evidence of benefit and carries the potential for serious harm, including death from hypocalcemia.
effect_size: No clinical-trial evidence of benefit; documented serious harm including fatal hypocalcemia; NIH trial cancelled on safety/ethics grounds
population: Cochrane systematic review (no eligible RCTs with usable benefit data)

provenance.primary: James S et al., 'Chelation for autism spectrum disorder (ASD)', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2015

confidence_notes: Flows from the false 'heavy metals cause autism' mechanism. Refuted and lethal. Cross-ref the broader 'detox for autism' category (secretin, HBOT, diets) which shares the same defect.

statement: MMS / 'Miracle Mineral Solution' (chlorine dioxide) is industrial bleach with zero evidence of benefit for autism and a clear mechanism of serious harm; ingesting it can be fatal.
effect_size: Documented caustic gut injury, acute liver failure, life-threatening dehydration, hemolysis; FDA and global regulators warn it can be fatal; sellers prosecuted

provenance.primary: US FDA consumer warnings on Miracle Mineral Solution / chlorine dioxide; multiple national regulator alerts; criminal prosecutions of sellers

confidence_notes: Not an 'unproven therapy' to be balanced — it is poison marketed as medicine, given to children orally and by enema. The shed bowel lining promoters call 'parasites' is caustic injury. Child-safety issue.

statement: The large rise in measured autism prevalence (to ~1 in 36 US 8-year-olds, 2020) is overwhelmingly attributable to broadened diagnostic criteria, awareness, ascertainment, diagnostic substitution, and service access — not a true biological epidemic.
effect_size: Prevalence ~1 in 150 (early 2000s) -> 1 in 36 (2020); most of the change tracks criteria/ascertainment changes
population: CDC ADDM network surveillance, 8-year-olds across multiple US sites

provenance.primary: Maenner MJ et al., 'Prevalence and Characteristics of Autism Spectrum Disorder Among Children Aged 8 Years', MMWR Surveill Summ 2023

confidence_notes: Does not foreclose small environmental contributions (advanced parental age, prematurity) but those do not explain the trend. Autism heritability is high (~50-90%); it is strongly genetic and polygenic.

statement: There is no treatment that makes an autistic child 'not autistic'; the evidence-based supports are early developmental/behavioral intervention, speech/OT, education, and treating co-occurring conditions, which improve function and quality of life.
effect_size: Early intervention improves developmental/functional outcomes vs later; no cure exists

provenance.primary: Developmental-intervention literature; AAP/CDC developmental-surveillance guidance (M-CHAT screening)

confidence_notes: Early-intervention efficacy is well supported though effect sizes and methods vary. The neurodiversity framing (difference to support, not defect to erase) is taken seriously alongside attention to genuine co-occurring medical conditions.

statement: Down syndrome life expectancy rose from ~25 years (1980s) to ~60 with modern cardiac surgery and medical care — a transformation driven by care, not by altering the genetics.
effect_size: ~25 -> ~60 years median life expectancy over ~four decades

provenance.primary: Antonarakis SE et al., 'Down syndrome', Nat Rev Dis Primers 2020

confidence_notes: Model case of Rule 1: unchangeable cause (trisomy 21), very changeable outcome (care). ~50% have congenital heart defects; chr-21 carries APP, raising early Alzheimer's risk. Majority of Down births are to mothers under 35 by sheer numbers.

statement: CFTR modulator therapy (elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor / Trikafta) produces large, sustained improvements in lung function in cystic fibrosis patients with at least one Phe508del allele, changing the natural history of the disease.
effect_size: Large gains in ppFEV1 and sweat chloride vs placebo, sustained
population: CF patients with a single Phe508del allele (and other modulator-eligible genotypes)

provenance.primary: Middleton PG et al., 'Elexacaftor-Tezacaftor-Ivacaftor for Cystic Fibrosis with a Single Phe508del Allele', NEJM 2019

confidence_notes: Transformative but not universal: modulators do not fit every CFTR mutation, and global access is deeply unequal. A single-gene 'recipe' corrected at the protein level. Sickle cell parallel owned by Section 31.

statement: Childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia, near-uniformly fatal in 1960, is now cured in roughly 90% of children with risk-stratified multi-agent chemotherapy plus CNS prophylaxis.
population: Children with ALL, cooperative-group trial era

provenance.primary: Inaba H, Greaves M, Mullighan CG, 'Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia', Lancet 2013; modern cooperative-group protocols

confidence_notes: Achieved by decades of incremental cooperative-group RCTs, not one drug. Survival is not uniform (some subtypes/regions/relapse remain hard) and survivorship late effects (cardiac, endocrine, neurocognitive, second cancers) are the new frontier.

statement: Type 1 diabetes is autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta-cells and is not caused by diet, sugar, or weight; it is biologically distinct from type 2 diabetes.

provenance.primary: Standard immunology/endocrinology consensus; teplizumab (anti-CD3) delayed clinical onset in at-risk relatives (Herold KC et al., NEJM 2019, 10.1056/NEJMoa1902226)

confidence_notes: Kills the hurtful 'they ate too much sugar' myth aimed at families. Management transformed by CGM + closed-loop systems; teplizumab is the first disease-modifying immunotherapy (delays, not prevents). Owned by Section 22.

statement: Prone (front) infant sleeping carries roughly 4-fold higher SIDS risk; the 'Back to Sleep' supine-positioning campaign roughly halved or more SIDS rates where adopted.
effect_size: Prone vs supine OR ~4-5x; SIDS rates fell ~50%+ post-campaign; review concluded earlier translation could have prevented tens of thousands of deaths
population: Systematic review of observational SIDS studies

provenance.primary: Gilbert R et al., 'Infant sleeping position and the sudden infant death syndrome: systematic review', Int J Epidemiol 2005

confidence_notes: Archetypal free, behavioral, high-leverage public-health win (Rule 3). Safe-sleep bundle adds firm flat surface, no soft bedding, room-share without bed-share, no overheating/smoke, breastfeeding/pacifier protective. Swaddling nuanced (Pease Pediatrics 2016, 10.1542/peds.2015-3275).

statement: Newborn screening (the heel-prick blood spot) detects asymptomatic treatable conditions such as PKU in the window where early treatment prevents irreversible damage; PKU, untreated, causes severe intellectual disability fully preventable by an early low-phenylalanine diet.
effect_size: Untreated PKU -> severe irreversible intellectual disability; early diet -> near-normal development; modern tandem-MS panels catch dozens of IEMs

provenance.primary: Guthrie bacterial-inhibition assay (1960s) and successor newborn-screening programs; PKU dietary-treatment evidence base

confidence_notes: Among the highest cost-effectiveness programs in medicine; the proof-of-concept that justifies the whole newborn-screening enterprise. Caveat: PKU diet is lifelong; maternal PKU (off-diet in pregnancy) can harm an unaffected fetus.

statement: Neural tube defects (anencephaly, spina bifida) result from failure of neural tube closure by ~week 4 and are substantially preventable by periconceptional folic acid and mandatory flour fortification.
effect_size: Periconceptional folic acid cut NTD recurrence ~72% (MRC); population NTD rates fell sharply post-fortification
population: MRC Vitamin Study (RCT) + population fortification cohorts

provenance.primary: MRC Vitamin Study Research Group, 'Prevention of neural tube defects', Lancet 1991
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed E-utilities verified (PMID 1677062); intervention graded in Section 19 (3.1)

confidence_notes: Section 43 covers the disease (spina bifida spectrum); Section 19 grades the folate intervention. Must be on board before pregnancy is known (tube closes ~wk 4). One of the great public-health wins.

statement: Cerebral palsy is a permanent movement disorder from a non-progressive injury to the developing brain (~2-3 per 1000 births); intelligence is often normal, and 'birth asphyxia' is over-blamed relative to prenatal factors and prematurity.
effect_size: Prevalence ~2-3/1000 live births; many cases trace to prenatal/prematurity causes rather than delivery events
population: Systematic review / meta-analysis of CP prevalence studies

provenance.primary: Oskoui M et al., 'An update on the prevalence of cerebral palsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis', Dev Med Child Neurol 2013

confidence_notes: Static lesion, dynamic clinical picture. Common harmful misconception that CP implies intellectual disability (it frequently does not). The asphyxia narrative has driven evidence-poor litigation.

statement: Prenatal screening tests (cell-free DNA / NIPT, combined screening) estimate probability, not diagnosis; for rare conditions their positive predictive value can be low, so a positive screen warrants a diagnostic test rather than action.
effect_size: NIPT high sensitivity for common trisomies but variable/low PPV for rare conditions; diagnostic confirmation (amniocentesis/CVS) required

provenance.primary: Prenatal-testing performance literature and professional-society counseling standards (non-directive counseling)
provenance.surfaced_via: Section 43 synthesis; cross-ref Section 18 testing ethics

confidence_notes: Marketing that blurs screen-vs-diagnosis has caused harm (terminations on false positives). Professional standard is non-directive counseling; disability-rights critiques are a serious part of the honest conversation.

statement: Rising childhood obesity is the developmental face of an obesogenic environment, genetics, and metabolic biology (including prenatal programming), not simply willpower or bad parenting; it brings forward adult-onset conditions like adolescent type 2 diabetes.
effect_size: Steep multi-decade prevalence rise; childhood obesity tracks into adulthood and forward to T2D, NAFLD, hypertension

provenance.primary: Pediatric obesity epidemiology and guidelines (family-based behavioral intervention; emerging GLP-1 / bariatric in adolescents)
provenance.surfaced_via: Section 43 synthesis; cross-ref Domain D / metabolic

confidence_notes: Stigmatizing families is cruel and counterproductive. Treatment landscape shifting and contested: adolescent pharmacotherapy (GLP-1) and bariatric surgery are a live evidence-vs-values debate. DOHaD link to Section 19.

statement: Early introduction of peanut (4-11 months) in high-risk infants dramatically reduces peanut allergy versus avoidance, reversing prior 'delay allergenic foods' advice.
effect_size: Large relative reduction in peanut allergy at age 5 with early introduction (LEAP)
population: High-risk infants (severe eczema and/or egg allergy)

provenance.primary: Du Toit G et al. (LEAP trial), 'Randomized trial of peanut consumption in infants at risk for peanut allergy', NEJM 2015

confidence_notes: Model case of pediatric folklore reversed by RCT. Graded in allergy/immunology domain; flagged here in the childhood asthma/allergy context.
